title: X is replacing revenue sharing with a new original content rewards program
excerpt: X, the social media platform formerly known as Twitter, is making significant changes to its monetization…
body:
X, the social media platform formerly known as Twitter, is making significant changes to its monetization strategy by retiring its existing revenue-sharing program in favor of a new original content rewards initiative. This shift marks a notable transformation in how creators can earn income on the platform.

What happened

As of September 7, X will officially discontinue its current revenue-sharing program. The platform has announced plans to replace this model with a new rewards program aimed specifically at creators who produce original content. The details surrounding the new program have not been fully disclosed, but it is expected to offer different incentives and support for content creators, reflecting X’s evolving approach to monetization. This change comes as part of X’s broader strategy to enhance user engagement and attract more creators to the platform.

Why it matters

The retirement of the revenue-sharing program signifies a pivotal shift in X’s approach to creator monetization. The previous model allowed creators to earn a portion of the ad revenue generated from their content, fostering a competitive environment for content production. However, the new rewards program could potentially redefine how creators interact with the platform and monetize their work. By focusing on original content, X aims to encourage higher-quality contributions and differentiate itself in a crowded social media landscape.

This change also highlights the ongoing evolution of social media platforms as they seek to adapt to the needs of creators and audiences alike. As competition intensifies among platforms, offering attractive monetization options has become crucial for retaining and attracting talent. X’s new initiative may serve as a strategic move to bolster its creator community and enhance user experience, ultimately impacting the platform’s growth and sustainability.

In conclusion, X’s decision to phase out its revenue-sharing program in favor of a new original content rewards initiative reflects a significant shift in its monetization strategy. As the platform seeks to attract more creators and improve content quality, the implications of this change will be closely watched by both creators and users.

Source: engadget.com.
